theme: 3 terms on breaking retain cycles: the number ARC tracks, a reference that turns nil, and a reference that assumes the object is always there

terms.definition: A number that tracks how many Strong References point to a class instance.
terms.example: The Reference Count of `Song` never hits zero, so it stays in memory.
terms.code:
class Song { deinit { print("Song freed") } }
var a: Song? = Song()   // count: 1
var b = a               // count: 2
a = nil                 // count: 1
b = nil                 // count: 0

terms.definition: A reference that does not keep an instance alive and turns into `nil` when the instance is freed.
terms.example: Make `delegate` a Weak Reference, so the screen can be freed.

terms.definition: A reference that does not keep an instance alive and assumes the instance is still there whenever it is used.
terms.example: `owner` is an Unowned Reference, because a `Card` never outlives its `User`.

quizzes.question: What reference does not keep an object alive, and crashes if you use it after the object is gone?

video.description:
Learn to explain how to break a retain cycle in Swift: Reference Count, Weak Reference & Unowned Reference, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Reference Count - A number that tracks how many Strong References point to a class instance.
Weak Reference - A reference that does not keep an instance alive and turns into `nil` when the instance is freed.
Unowned Reference - A reference that does not keep an instance alive and assumes the instance is still there whenever it is used.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain weak and unowned in English?

dialogue.title: Weak or unowned?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I added `weak` to `lead`, and now `Dev freed` prints!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. `lead` is a Weak Reference now, so it doesn't keep `Dev` alive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Reference Count of `Dev` can reach zero again?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. A Weak Reference doesn't add to the Reference Count.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then what happens to `lead` after `Dev` is freed?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It turns into `nil` by itself. That's why it has to be optional.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not an Unowned Reference? It looks simpler.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An Unowned Reference assumes `Dev` is always there. If it's gone, the app crashes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a team can lose its lead, so `weak` is safer here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Use an Unowned Reference only when the other object always lives longer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. When `deinit` never runs, check the Reference Count first.
When the Reference Count hits zero, the object is freed.
